samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` — the whole housekeeping surface — has no test at all
samples.evidence: `offline-runtime.tsx` (176 lines) is new and referenced only by `PrivateRoute.tsx:35`. I grepped `packages/frontend` for `offline-runtime|OfflineRuntime|offerRecoverableWork` and the only hits are the file itself and the import in PrivateRoute; `packages/frontend/tests` has no offline test files (only sync-status ones matched `offline`). Untested behaviour includes: `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` on mount and `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` on cleanup (which is what makes logout's erase find an identity at all — set wrongly, signing out silently leaves document content on a shared disk), the once-per-session `collectStale()` and its swallow, the `cancelled` getter guarding the await-between-items loop, skipping keys `describeArchivedDocument` cannot read, the `fetchDocument` title fallback, and every branch of the recovery toast (`refused === 'empty'` vs unreadable, `complete === false` wording, the navigate-on-Open action). `recoverOfflineCopy` and `listRecoverableWork` are well covered as units, but the component that decides when and whether they run is not covered anywhere.

samples.summary: The real Web Locks adapter (`webLocks()`) is never exercised; every election test injects a fake lock manager
samples.evidence: In `durable-session.test.ts` every call to `acquireDurableSession` is preceded by `setDurableLockForTest(fakeLocks())` (or by a `navigator.locks`-absent case where `supportsDurableSession()` is false and no request is made). `supportsDurableSession()` short-circuits to `true` whenever `injected` is set, so the `webLocks()` branch in `acquireDurableSession` is unreachable from the suite. That leaves the production code path untested: the `ifAvailable: true` callback contract, `resolve(undefined)` when `lock` is null, and — most importantly — the parked `new Promise<void>(resolveHeld => …)` that is what actually holds and later frees the lock. The `beforeAll` stub installed in the suite (`request: () => Promise.resolve(undefined)`) ignores the callback entirely, so it could not even be used to drive this path (a call would hang). If `webLocks()` is wrong, no tab ever becomes durable (feature dead) or the name is never released (every later tab refused), and the entire green suite of election tests would still pass.

verdict.reason: I could not find any counterexample: nothing in the repository exercises the real `webLocks()` adapter. `webLocks()` is module-private and reached only at durable-session.ts:151 via `(injected ?? webLocks())`, and `supportsDurableSession()` (durable-session.ts:57-60) short-circuits to true whenever `injected` is set. Every `acquireDurableSession` call in durable-session.test.ts (lines 97, 101, 115-116, 127-128, 141, 145, 154-155, 165, 168, 182) is preceded by `setDurableLockForTest` with an in-memory fake (test:38-48) or a rejecting stub (test:178-180); the two non-injecting cases (test:186-223) delete `navigator.locks` so no request is issued. Searching wider than the reviewer: the other durable suites also inject their own fakes (use-durable-document.test.tsx:24 fakeLocks + setDurableLockForTest at lines 48-421; collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:87-97,107). The `beforeAll` stub (test:15-25) supplies `request: () => Promise.resolve(undefined)`, which ignores the callback entirely and so could not drive the real path; the only `navigator.locks` spies (test:229,242,253,265,275) target `query`, i.e. `isOpenInAnyTab`. Repo-wide, `ifAvailable` occurs exactly once — durable-session.ts:93 — with zero test occurrences, and `wb-durable` appears only in source, the three injecting test files, wafflebase-doc-store.ts and a design doc. There is no e2e directory and no browser-mode/setup polyfill of Web Locks. So the ifAvailable contract, the `resolve(undefined)` null-lock branch, and the parked promise that holds and later frees the lock are untested; if wrong, durability is dead or the name is never released (every later tab refused) while the whole election suite stays green. In-lane (missing test over real behavior) and major by the rubric.

finding.summary: No test anywhere exercises the durable client against the real SDK provider/store, so the headline behaviour (unsent edits survive a reload) is unverified end to end
finding.evidence: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` mocks `@yorkie-js/react` wholesale (`YorkieProvider` merely pushes its props into a `mounted` array), so the assertions reach only as far as "these props were passed": `expect(mounted[0].clientKey).toBe('wb:7:note-7')` and `expect(mounted[0].store).toBeDefined()`. Nothing verifies the SDK accepts a `clientKey`/`store` pair, writes through `WafflebaseDocStore`, or that a reload under the same key resumes — and `packages/frontend/package.json:65` pins `@yorkie-js/react` to `0.7.22`, the version `supportsClientKey()` deliberately rejects, while the durable suite and `use-durable-document.test.tsx` both `vi.spyOn(capabilities, 'supportsClientKey').mockReturnValue(true)` in `beforeEach`. So the only configuration the feature is ever tested in is one that cannot exist in this build, and the store↔client seam has no coverage on either side of the mock. I searched `packages/frontend/tests` and for a browser/integration lane and found none (`Grep -i 'WafflebaseDocStore|clientKey|offline'` in tests matches only the three sync-status files).

verdict.reason: The finding's central absence claim — that the store↔client seam has no coverage on either side of the mock and that "unsent edits survive" is never exercised against the real SDK — is contradicted by tests in the repo. `doc-store-contract.ts` is the SDK's own DocStore contract (transcribed at v0.7.22) and `wafflebase-doc-store.test.ts:15-23` runs it against both WafflebaseDocStore and the SDK's published MemoryDocStore, so drift from upstream fails against upstream's own implementation. `offline-copy.test.ts:34-97` and `offline-copy-recovery.test.ts:75-132,271-435` drive real `@yorkie-js/sdk` `Document` objects: snapshot via `doc.toBytes()`, the post-snapshot unsent change appended into WafflebaseDocStore, then rebuilt through real `Document.fromBytes`/`restoreAppendedChanges` and asserted to contain the offline edit — precisely the "unsent edits are not lost" behaviour, against real SDK code rather than a mock. The claim that "the only configuration the feature is ever tested in is one that cannot exist in this build" is also inverted: `yorkie-capabilities.test.ts:23-25` asserts 0.7.22 → false and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:199-206` asserts nothing mounts when the build cannot carry a key — that is the build's actual configuration. Because `useDurableDocument` gates `eligible` on `supportsClientKey()` (use-durable-document.ts:115-120) and the pin is 0.7.22 (package.json:65), the durable client cannot mount in this build at all, so the one genuinely absent piece (mounting the real YorkieProvider with clientKey/store against a live server) is a path no user can reach here and whose dependency version is not even installed. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is not a behaviour change left without meaningful tests.

finding.summary: No test covers the `saved-locally` state ever reaching the chip — `useSyncStatus` never passes `durable`
finding.evidence: `deriveSyncState` gained a `durable` input and a new `saved-locally` state (sync-state.ts:70-85), and `tests/components/sync-status/sync-state.test.ts` exercises the pure function. But the only production caller, `use-sync-status.ts:214`, calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed })` with no `durable` argument, and nothing else in src computes it. So the entire user-facing value of the feature is unreachable in the app and no test would fail. The chip suite (`tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx`) has no case for `saved-locally`, and its existing case 'does not claim the work is stored locally' (line 379) still passes precisely because durability never arrives.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual premise and its absence claim both fail. (1) The sole production caller does pass durability: use-sync-status.ts:3 imports `useDocumentDurability`, line 75 reads it, and line 220 calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed, durable })` — the reviewer's quoted "line 214 ... with no `durable` argument" is not what the file contains. (2) A hook-level test for the reachability of `saved-locally` exists: tests/components/sync-status/use-sync-status.test.ts:403-432 renders the real `useSyncStatus` inside a real `DurableDocumentScope` with `durable: true`, drives a local edit while `connection: 'disconnected'`, and asserts `result.current.state === 'saved-locally'`; the paired case at 434-461 asserts `'not-saved'` under `durable: false`, so the assertion discriminates on the feature rather than holding unconditionally. (3) A chip-level test exists too: tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:418-472 (`describe('SyncStatusChip on a durable document')`) uses the `renderDurableChip` helper at lines 93-107 to mount the real `SyncStatusChip` under a real `DurableDocumentScope`, and asserts the rendered text `'Saved to this device'` (the label mapped from `'saved-locally'` at sync-status-chip.tsx:41), the absence of `'Not saved'`, no destructive styling, `aria-live="polite"`, and that neither the toast warning nor the beforeunload guard fires. Only `@yorkie-js/react` and `sonner` are mocked; the state machine, hook, context and chip are all real, so these tests would fail if `durable` stopped flowing. The finding's claim that the chip suite "has no case for saved-locally" is directly contradicted.

finding.summary: New chip state `saved-locally` (label, icon, tooltip, and the deliberate absence of the warning toast / unload guard) has no chip-level test
finding.evidence: sync-status-chip.tsx adds LABELS['saved-locally'], ICONS['saved-locally'] and a bespoke tooltip paragraph, and `stranded`/`mayHaveUnsent` (lines 106-109) deliberately exclude the new state so no beforeunload prompt, navigation guard or red toast fires. None of that is asserted anywhere: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` contains no `saved-locally` case. If the state were wired up wrongly (e.g. it kept the destructive styling, or lost the guard for work that is not actually durable) nothing in the suite would fail.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the `saved-locally` chip state (label, non-destructive presentation, and the deliberate absence of the warning toast / unload guard) has no chip-level test. The chip test file contains a dedicated `describe('SyncStatusChip on a durable document')` block (sync-status-chip.test.tsx:418-487) that renders SyncStatusChip inside `DurableDocumentScope` with `durable: true` against a disconnected, pending fake doc — which deriveSyncState (sync-state.ts:75-86) resolves precisely to 'saved-locally'. It asserts the label 'Saved to this device' and absence of 'Not saved' (430-431), that the chip carries no `destructive` styling (434-436), `aria-live="polite"` rather than assertive (451-453), and — after advancing past the 2s toast debounce — that no warning toast fired and that the net count of registered `beforeunload` listeners is 0 (456-472, using the `unloadGuards()` helper at 112-117), i.e. exactly the `stranded`/`mayHaveUnsent` exclusion at sync-status-chip.tsx:106-109. A further case pins that durability does not alter the in-flight 'Saving' row (474-486). The reviewer's literal grep for 'saved-locally' missed these because the tests drive the state through the real DurableDocumentScope seam instead of naming the union member. Only the exact tooltip wording and the IconDeviceDesktop identity are unasserted, which is narrower cosmetic coverage, not the claimed absence, and does not meet the major bar.

finding.summary: Recovery only tested for `sheet`; the `doc`, `slides`, `board` and `note` rebuild paths are untested
finding.evidence: `readContent` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:39-86) has branches for doc/slides/board built on YorkieDocStore/YorkieSlidesStore/YorkieBoardStore, and `writeNote` (line ~147) handles notes via a live `Client`. `offline-copy-recovery.test.ts` only ever archives a sheet-shaped root and calls with `type: 'sheet'` (plus an 'image' refusal and an unreadable archive). A wrong reader for doc/slides/board would hand the user an empty or plausible-but-wrong 'offline copy' of work that the SDK already dropped — the last copy of it — and no test would catch it. The note path is not executed at all.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing tests exist. offline-copy-recovery.test.ts:270-462 is a `describe("rebuilding each document type")` block covering all four paths: doc (:271-317, seeded through YorkieDocStore, asserts rebuilt inline text contains the post-snapshot "offline" edit), slides (:319-361, asserts slide ids ["s1","s2"]), board (:363-403, asserts elements ids ["e1"]), and note (:405-435, asserts created payload {title:"Ideas (offline copy)", type:"note"}, that `applied` stays empty because notes bypass applyImportedContent, and that the text written into the attached doc contains both "# Title" and "typed offline"), plus a note-rebuilt-empty refusal (:437-461, expects refused==="empty", nothing created, archive kept). These exercise readContent's doc/slides/board branches (offline-copy-recovery.ts:54-80), readNote (:91-94) and writeNote (:199-219). The tests are not over-mocked: @yorkie-js/sdk is mocked via importOriginal with only Client replaced (test:11-25), so the real Document and the real Yorkie*Store readers run; the shared archiveDocument helper (test:110-132) writes an edit after the snapshot so a reader that ignored the replayed log would fail. The finding's stated evidence ("only ever archives a sheet-shaped root and calls with type: 'sheet'", "the note path is not executed at all") is contradicted by the file in the working tree.

finding.summary: No test asserts the durable store is constructed with the cross-tab `isOpenElsewhere` guard
finding.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` builds `new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId, isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab })` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:77-88), and the store's own suite (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts, 'documents open in another tab') shows that without that callback one tab's eviction/sweep deletes another tab's open document and its later appends silently vanish. The only component-level assertion is `expect(mounted[0].store).toBeDefined()` in collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx, which holds for any object — including a store constructed without `isOpenElsewhere` or with the wrong `userId`. The wiring that prevents cross-tab data loss is therefore untested.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists in the same file the reviewer read. collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:266-301 ('the cross-tab guard' > 'builds the store with a liveness check that can see other tabs') spies on the real `session.isOpenInAnyTab`, mounts the provider, takes the store the provider actually constructed (`mounted[0].store`), writes an untouched entry via a second REAL WafflebaseDocStore over the same database (`store.databaseName`), runs the real `store.collectStale(0)`, then asserts `expect(openElsewhere).toHaveBeenCalledWith('sheet-9')` and that the other tab's document survives (`expect(await reader.load('sheet-9')).toBeDefined()`). Those assertions fail if `isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab` is dropped from the constructor at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:88-95, since `isLive` would then return false and collectStale would delete the entry (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:291-311). The store is not mocked (only @yorkie-js/react and @tanstack/react-query are), and it runs on fake-indexeddb, so this is real, non-vacuous coverage of the exact cross-tab data-loss wiring. The reviewer's claim that `expect(mounted[0].store).toBeDefined()` (line 134) is the only component-level assertion does not hold against the working tree.
